thread: The sick village after the party leaves: the patients, the missing flour, Joss and the ledger

evidence.clue: Dawn status: Elsie cool; cooper's boy awake and asking for bread; Col perfectly well and going home; Wenna asleep, forehead 'a sleeper's warmth'; Garran unchanged, dry, hot, the brown still out along his arms and up his neck.

Flour: granary and bakehouse burned; Piers, his brother and the Aldon boys go door to door on the near side of the brook collecting every sack and crock from anyone who has bought since harvest; 'Most of them' done at midnight, Brask still going round; the cart to the ford turned round by Dickon (the Hallams hadn't unloaded; the alehouse had two sacks), the load burned; the loft boards and Jaina's ice burned.

Unknown: whether the village has flour held in houses on the far side of the brook or the top farm; whether Mag (flushed, coughing at the egg stall) and others are sick; whether the contamination in the ground and water persists; whether Joss is dupe or accomplice.
Brask intends to question Joss and 'go through the loft in daylight'; takes the party's four names in his ledger 'If anyone comes asking what happened here, I want to tell it right'.

Tobin keeps feeding Garran Mother Haw's oatcake in milk; the wards are left to thin once Jaina leaves ('the wards would hold a while on their own now'); she gives the cases no more than 'oats, if anybody brings you oats'.

readerKnows: The village lives for now; the early cases are recovering; the late case is stable; the party leaves without finishing the checks.
povCharacterKnows: Jaina: she has done what she could and will not see them again; she knows she cannot ward a village.
notes: Per plan, Brask does not return on page; his only later appearance is a sworn letter for the defence in Chapter 23 (the ledger of names). The village's name is never given. Do not kill or heal Garran off-page without a reason.
